title: Hyperbatch attention: deferred-rope fused QKV kernel and priority-aware scheduler
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in fused QKV+deferred-rope attention kernel and a priority-aware hyperbatch scheduler. Default behavior unchanged; opt-in via runtime flag. Improves median latency and tail for mixed small/long seq workloads and reduces per-token GPU memory pressure for streaming requests.
description:
Motivation: Production workloads at Redwood show a bimodal sequence length distribution (many short streaming requests interleaved with occasional long completions). Existing kernels either favor short requests (low setup overhead) or long requests (amortized compute) but we observe increased tail latency and suboptimal KV cache pressure when both are colocated. This PR introduces a combined approach: 1) a fused QKV kernel that applies rotary/rope as a deferred step during the attention compute path (reducing redundant memory shuffles); 2) a 'hyperbatch' scheduler that continuously batches compatible requests but prioritizes low-latency streaming tails and defers rope rematerialization for batched long sequences; 3) priority-aware KV cache admission/eviction policies so short high-qps sessions retain hot prefixes.

What changed (high-level):
- New fused kernel: runtime/attn/fused_deferred_rope.cu and runtime/attn/fused_deferred_rope.h implement a CUDA kernel that fuses q/k/v transpose, qkv interleave, and rotary application into a single pass when the runtime flag enable_fused_deferred_rope=true. The kernel applies rope by streaming position indices in-band so we avoid a separate pre-transform buffer for rotary keys when sequence optics permit.
- Hyperbatch scheduler: runtime/scheduler/hyperbatch_scheduler.cpp adds continuous-batching logic that groups requests by model variant, dtype, and effective rope-offset compatibility. The scheduler maintains a fast-path for <64-token streaming requests with strict latency SLOs and a deferred path for long sequences where rope application is delayed until the kernel's final combine stage.
- KV cache priorities: runtime/kv/priority_cache.cc implements a scored admission policy (recency + request_priority tag) and a spill strategy that prefers evicting low-priority long-session shards before short-session prefixes.
- API/flags: runtime/config/flags.h and docs/ops/flags.md add enable_fused_deferred_rope & scheduler.hyperbatch.enable toggles. Feature is opt-in and off by default for safety.
- Metrics and tracing: observability/metrics/attn_metrics.cc adds attn.kernel.fused_deferred_rope.invocations and scheduler.hyperbatch.batch_size histogram. Added traces for 'deferred_rope' decision points to the RPC trace context.
- Tests and harness changes: perf/bench/hyperbatch_end2end.yaml and tests/attn/test_fused_deferred_rope.cpp with unit and integration tests validating numeric parity with current pipeline and coverage for rope edge-cases (odd/even rotary dims, variable base indices).

Benchmarks: (internal perf harness on p4d.24xlarge, mixed workload: 80% short(<=64) streaming, 20% long(>512))
- Baseline (main): median latency p50=18.6ms, p95=210ms, throughput=14.2k tokens/s, GPU mem usage 24.8GB
- This PR (opt-in flags both enabled): median latency p50=14.2ms (-23%), p95=132ms (-37%), throughput=17.3k tokens/s (+22%), GPU mem usage 22.1GB (-11%)
- Long-only workloads show parity in token throughput (+1-3%) and slightly improved memory locality.

Correctness: Kernel reuses existing attention math and matches reference fp32 and fp16 outputs within numerical tolerance (L2 delta < 1e-5 on sampled tensors). Unit tests cover rotary edgecases and continuous-batching boundary conditions. Numeric tests run on CI and on a small nightly GPU matrix.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind two runtime flags and an operator-visible toggle in the console. Start with internal canary on dedicated pools, then staged rollout to hosted clusters with gradual traffic ramp and automatic rollback on regression alerts.
- Observability: new metrics and trace spans are included; Canary dashboards added in docs/ops/canaries.md.

Why this is different: Earlier PRs introduced fused QKV or rotary optimizations or scheduler tweaks independently. This PR focuses on integrating a deferred-rope strategy into a fused kernel specifically to reduce memory shuffles during continuous batching and pairs it with a scheduler and KV policy that prioritizes short low-latency sessions. The combined effect reduces tail latency under mixed workloads and lowers per-token overhead for streaming-heavy applications.

review_comments: Jinsoo Park requested changes: Please add a small fallback path for older GPUs with limited shared memory; the kernel currently assumes 64KB per CTA. Suggested to check SM capability at runtime and fallback to two-pass rope application.
Avery Chen (author) replied: Added a capability check and a two-pass fallback that keeps semantics identical. See fused_deferred_rope.cu: fallback_two_pass_apply_rope().
Maria Gonzales asked: Can we track how often deferred_rope was chosen vs. immediate rope in the first 10M requests? Add a counter.
Avery Chen: Added metric attn.deferred_rope.selection_count and a trace tag. Also added a perf harness flag to emit selection rates.
Liam O'Neill: Approves with comment: Nice work — please coordinate with release engineering for a staged rollout. Also ensure the priority scores are documented for SRE teams.
Release Engineering (comment): Confirmed gating flags and rollout timeline; requested a short postmortem runbook be added to docs/ops/canaries.md (done).
ci_checks: perf-regression: pass (no regressions on nightly long-only)
notes_for_ops: Feature is off by default. To enable: set runtime flag enable_fused_deferred_rope=true and scheduler.hyperbatch.enable=true on target pools. Monitor attn.kernel.fused_deferred_rope.invocations and scheduler.hyperbatch.batch_size; watch attn.deferred_rope.selection_count for distribution. If p95 increases after enabling, rollback the flags and open ENG-1429.
changelog_entry: opt-in: fused QKV kernel with deferred rope application and a hyperbatch scheduler to reduce tail latency for mixed streaming workloads (flags: enable_fused_deferred_rope, scheduler.hyperbatch.enable).
notes_for_reviewers: Numeric parity checks included; please focus on the fallback path for older GPUs and the KV priority scoring parameters. Perf numbers are reproducible via perf/bench/hyperbatch_end2end.yaml.
